captions.telegram: Twelve minutes to get the first wrap right, and nobody counted out loud.
captions.instagram: Hemp leaves a pattern that outlasts the afternoon. She said the boards were the worst part, then changed her mind about that too.
captions.email: Knees on board, shoulders wrapped. Tea went cold twice.

captions.telegram: Buckle first, then the long pause before anything else happens.
captions.instagram: Leather remembers a wrist. Three years of this cuff and it still asks for a firm hand on the tongue of the strap, every single time, without apology.
captions.email: One buckle. Everything after it was easier.

captions.telegram: Hotel silk, which is to say almost silk, sliding anyway.
captions.instagram: Room 704 had a mirror nobody asked for. The robe did what robes do around eleven at night. We stayed past the booking and paid for it gladly.
captions.email: Borrowed room, borrowed hour, honest robe.

captions.telegram: Tile at six in the morning is a negotiation you lose.
captions.instagram: Toes curl before the brain agrees to any of it. Cold underfoot, warm everywhere the light lands, and somewhere behind the camera a radiator finally clanks on.
captions.email: Chilly stone, curled toes, no complaints filed.

captions.telegram: Two flames, one of them a lie the glass tells.
captions.instagram: Wax pooled while nobody watched the clock. Her back turned away and the reflection stayed, which felt like standing in two rooms at once.
captions.email: Candle, mirror, shoulder blades. That was the evening.

captions.telegram: Forearms doing arithmetic nobody ever taught them.
captions.instagram: A single column looks simple until your hands have to do it under someone else's breathing. Four tries tonight. The fourth one held, and that is a fine ratio.
captions.email: Four attempts, one knot worth keeping.

captions.telegram: Glass between us, and the weather taking her side.
captions.instagram: Rain does the editing for free. Through the pane she is mostly suggestion, a dark slip and a shoulder, and the droplet running sideways is the only thing in focus.
captions.email: Wet pane. A slip. Focus lost on purpose.

captions.telegram: Peeling latex makes a sound the microphone refused to take seriously.
captions.instagram: Matte until it stretches, then suddenly not matte at all. The forearm underneath ran warmer than anyone predicted, which surprised nobody who has worn these.
captions.email: Glove off, slowly, for the sound of it.

captions.telegram: The collar stayed on the sheets, which says plenty.
captions.instagram: Nobody wears it in this frame and that is the point. A bed nobody made, a strap nobody put away, and a Sunday that ran out before either got done.
captions.email: An empty collar on rumpled sheets.

captions.telegram: Velvet, an arch, and a chaise older than both of us.
captions.instagram: Furniture from 1930 has opinions about posture. Arms above the head until the shoulders protested, then a stretch, then the same shape again because it was worth repeating.
captions.email: Old velvet held the shape an hour.

captions.telegram: Knee braced against the frame, laces pulled past comfortable.
captions.instagram: Lacing is half the ritual and nobody photographs it. Eyelet by eyelet up the calf, a knot at the top, and only then does the rest of the night get to begin.
captions.email: Laces tight. Evening allowed to start.

captions.telegram: Blinds do to a torso what a ruler does to paper.
captions.instagram: Six stripes, then seven when she moved. Afternoon light is a free lighting rig with terrible manners and better instincts than most of my equipment.
captions.email: Bands of afternoon across a ribcage.

captions.telegram: A hand at the nape, relaxed, which is the difficult part.
captions.instagram: Pressure is easy. Resting there without gripping took more practice than any knot in this account, and it reads instantly to anyone who has been on the other side.
captions.email: Fingers resting, not holding. Harder than it looks.

captions.telegram: One pulled thread and the whole leg becomes a map.
captions.instagram: A snag is not damage, it is a timestamp. Somewhere between the second drink and the taxi this thread gave up, and the rest of the night went better for it.
captions.email: Snagged at the thigh. Worn anyway.

captions.telegram: Neither of them touching, and the doorway holding both.
captions.instagram: The distance in this frame was measured, not accidental. Two outlines, a threshold, and about eleven seconds before somebody moved first.
captions.email: Two shapes, one threshold, no contact yet.

captions.telegram: Half a harness and a coil waiting its turn.
captions.instagram: Unfinished work photographs better than finished work. The coil on the boards is the second half of a plan we abandoned for a nap, which was the correct call.
captions.email: Partly built, then abandoned for a nap.

captions.telegram: Smudged past the line, looking at something behind me.
captions.instagram: Nothing here is looking back. Colour past the edge of the lip, attention somewhere left of the lens, and I did not ask what she was watching.
captions.email: Colour past the lip line. Eyes elsewhere.

captions.telegram: Wrists crossed, nothing holding them, which is its own knot.
captions.instagram: No rope in this one. Hands behind the back because she put them there and left them, and anyone who has done that knows how loud an absent restraint gets.
captions.email: Crossed wrists. Nothing binding them at all.

captions.telegram: A handprint wiped through the fog, already closing again.
captions.instagram: Bathroom mirrors keep a record for about ninety seconds. Five fingers dragged across it, a stripe of the real room behind, then steam takes the evidence back.
captions.email: Five fingers through the steam. Gone by now.

captions.telegram: Two shoes, one upright, the hallway unbothered.
captions.instagram: Whatever happened here happened fast enough to leave footwear behind. One standing, one on its side, and a corridor that has seen this before.
captions.email: Shoes left mid-hallway, one on its side.
